scope: Perimeter values for the complete coupled corpus field. A corpus bound comes from the register or the corrected DOCX and may not be changed by a run. A fixture parameter has no corpus bound: every run must declare its own range for it in the manifest, and the gate refuses a value outside that declared range. Units are experiment units until calibrated (C07, C09). Bounds are inclusive unless exclusive_min or exclusive_max is true; null means unbounded on that side.

n.note: grid size; a numerical fixture, never a corpus quantity; 8 is the smallest grid the filtered pseudospectral scheme resolves

max_dt.note: requested cap on the time step; the solver's stability cap may realise a smaller step, and that cap is an added fixture rule the manifest must state; never a corpus quantity

initial_total.note: total initial S mass placed on the grid; a fixture

A0.note: accumulator prehistory A(0); C03: unknown prehistory is not zero, so a run declares a value and a range

sigma.note: sigma >= 0; sigma > 0 makes the tanh tail reverse direction

epsilon.note: epsilon > 0; sets the tanh and smooth exact-off scales

delta.note: delta > 0; shifts the onset to sqrt(Gamma^2 + 2 delta Gamma) unless the calibrated form is used

h.note: kernel width; the kernel must integrate to 1

mu0.note: mu0 > 0; mu0 = rho nu is a closure a run must declare (C07)

gamma.note: no corpus sign or magnitude; declare a range

kappa.note: no corpus sign or magnitude; declare a range

law.note: three distinct laws; no fourth may be added without an added-rule entry

gradient_law.note: the three gradient measures named in the register

hard_stops: A parameter missing from this file is an undeclared rule: refuse the run and add it here or as an added rule in the manifest.
A corpus-sourced parameter outside its bound is refused; the bound cannot be edited by a run manifest.
A fixture-sourced parameter with no declared range in the manifest is refused; silence about a range is a silent assumption.
A value outside its declared fixture range is refused even when it would compute.
A law or gradient_law outside the register's choices is refused; a new law is an added rule with its own name.
